1.why: Screens use a clean sans-serif face at a comfortable size with roomy line spacing and clear label/body hierarchy, though monospace code strings and the small grey Logs text are less generously spaced.

2.why: All instructions are short single sentences in sentence case with no italics, no all-caps prose (only code values and 'TESTING ONLY' log labels), and no dense paragraphs.

3.why: The single-column card layout with full-width buttons and large touch targets scales well to a phone; only the two-column backup-code grid and long setup key/log strings risk cramping on a narrow screen.

4.why: Every step uses plain, brief wording such as 'Check it is you', 'Keep these codes somewhere safe. Each code works once.'

5.why: Placeholders and hints show expected input formats: 'marcus@example.com', '123456' for OTP fields, 'ABCD-EFGH-IJKL' for the backup code, plus 'The code has 6 numbers, like 123456.'

6.why: No screen presents more than a couple of short lines before the primary action; the longest block is a three-line reassurance note.

7.why: 'Copy setup key' is offered for the TOTP secret and 'Copy all codes' for the backup codes, so long secrets need not be typed.

8.why: Step 5 displays a scannable QR code above the setup key as an explicit alternative to manual entry.

9.why: Standard labelled email/password inputs suggest autofill would work, but nothing visible (e.g. autocomplete hints, one-time-code affordances) confirms password-manager or OTP autofill support.

10.why: A 'Step X of 5' indicator with the number highlighted sits above each card, and a single high-contrast blue filled button dominates each screen.

11.why: Each screen has one clear primary action, though some steps also expose secondary buttons ('Send a new code', 'Get a new practice code', 'Show setup key again') alongside it.

12.why: Confirmations appear plainly ('Setup complete.', 'MFA is ready — Your authenticator is connected and backup codes are saved') and headings signal the next task, though intermediate steps rely more on the new heading than an explicit 'that worked' message.

13.why: The flow provides 'Send a new code', 'Get a new practice code', 'Show setup key again', 'Hide key', 'Show my codes again' and states 'Retries have no penalty.'

14.why: The sign-in error reads 'We could not sign you in. Check your email and password, then try again.' — non-blaming with a fix, but it is generic rather than specifying which field is wrong.

15.why: Text explicitly states 'There is no rush' and 'There is no time limit for reading or retries', and no countdown, timer or auto-refresh element appears on any screen.
